AI Credits

AI credits billing system across Business Manager and Wixel

2026 · Monetisation

Wix was rolling out AI features across the platform. Those features consumed credits. The design problem sounds simple: show users their balance, but it isn't: a billing concept that lives across three surfaces, two user tiers, and multiple plan states, with real consequences if someone misunderstands mid-task.

What I Did

Mapping the model

  • The tricky part was that free and premium users had completely different mental models: free users think "how much do I have today?" and premium users think "what did I pay for?"
  • The component also had to work consistently across three surfaces: Business Manager, Wixel (desktop and mobile), and AI vertical pages

Designing the system

  • Designed a two-tier credit wallet to match each mental model
  • The same component skeleton had to adapt to both the Business Manager and Wixel design systems, and be available as a standalone widget and as a widget embedded inside a page
  • Defined the full state space: low credits, empty, paywall triggers, upgrade prompts, and notifications
  • Explored a collaborator wallet (scoped out, not shipped)

Cross-functional and content

  • Partnered with Premium, AI verticals, and Legal on scope and monetization
  • Owned content for the project, briefing UX writers and approving final copy

Impact

Credits consumption grew significantly post-launch. The signal I was actually tracking was quieter, no support escalations, no confusion around the billing model. For infrastructure design, invisibility is the goal.

Behind the scenes

Bottom line

Billing infrastructure is one of those surfaces where design is almost invisible when it works, and loudly broken when it doesn't. The challenge here wasn't making it beautiful; it was making it legible: a user should be able to understand their credit state at a glance and know exactly what to do next. Getting that right required as much work on the mental model as on the interface itself.
